feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. This is the final iteration, so no later geometry change can follow. The candidate is the iteration 7 and 9 design (score 75.9247, reproduced exactly), and the controller is unchanged from iterations 3 to 9. Controller compensation: none is needed on the development tracks. The gains and 25-per-metre weights are the ones that produced the oval gain at y = 0.08. Iteration 8 (mass 0.5) dropped oval progress from 0.2725 to 0.12, and iteration 10 (wheel_track 0.11) dropped the score to 54.95. Both tests show that this design is sensitive to single parameters. The result on the unseen track is not measured and is not predicted here. Its outcome will depend on how far the track shape differs from the development tracks. If the team gets a later iteration, the race data should be read per track: a low s-bend or slalom result with few line losses points to the lead (y = 0.08, the maximum), and high steering oscillation with completion intact points to turn authority (wheel_track). Apply those changes only if the evidence supports them.
